claims.claim: The kit's evaluation config rebuilds the environment and task from the checkpoint's own resolved config (use_checkpoint_config is true) and evaluates with deterministic actions.

The kit's example batch runner evaluates each episode's checkpoint with one world by default, and all three Track 2 tiers are configured with one world per episode, all episodes scored and a private fraction of 0.

In the exported object trajectory the reference_frame column equals the rollout step plus the start frame and time_s equals the step divided by the control rate, and the kit reads the submission frame index from reference_frame.

The packer requires a row for every reference frame of every scored episode in each expected world, and the public sample submission has a single world with 553 contiguous frames (0 to 552) for episode 20.
The kit's evaluator must run with the FlashCHORD runtime at upstream commit aee95f25ae, because the public v0.4.0 release lacks the trajectory export.
On the Track 2 leaderboard SP-SR and MP-SR are fractions of episodes judged by each episode's mean position and orientation errors, and each metric is averaged across episodes.
A Track 2 submission must include a trajectory for every scored episode, produced with one checkpoint per episode.
The accepted evaluator script and evaluator code hash lists in config/tracks.json are currently empty.

Since a submitted row's frame index is simply the rollout step, a real-time-playback ep20 policy, whose rollout runs 921 steps, would have its steps 0 to 552 scored against reference frames 0 to 552, whereas the frame-by-frame ep20 policy runs exactly 553 steps, one per reference frame.
The public Track 2 sample submission covers 30 episodes.
The kit's example batch runner evaluates each episode with 4096 worlds by default.
The kit converts time_s into a 30 frames-per-second frame index before matching rows to the reference.
